A frame rejected for low laplacian variance is therefore reported to the caller as a clean board. In defect inspection that is a false negative: a blank frame or camera fault reads as a part with no defects.
Latency was measured on random-noise frames: P50 42.746ms, P95 47.162ms, P99 48.927ms. That bounds compute cost and says nothing about detection accuracy, which needs labelled frames.
The multi-camera figure is a sequential microbenchmark, so it does not establish behaviour under thread or process contention.

limitations: F3 now PASSES (PASS) — the contract gate was made fail-closed, so the validator no longer lets a malformed row reach KPI math. The earlier 'F3 FAILS' defect entry in this matrix was stale and has been removed rather than kept as a live defect.

Deployed by digest, not tag: revision ca-factory-api--0000002 references sha256:7c3e81b7… and the SLSA attestation resolves to git commit be4ace3, so commit -> workflow run -> digest -> revision -> probe is a closed chain.

The quality gate is VERIFIED on the live Azure revision: the probed report response carries generation_mode=FALLBACK, quality.status=GOOD with 5/5 checks ok, an evidence snapshot_id and 13 provenance ids with provenance_rejected=0. Defect Q1 (cumulative-DLQ quarantine rate, fixed at be4ace3) is closed and re-verified in the cloud: 10 consecutive ETL refreshes, each {'success': true}, left the rate flat at 0.009 with scope=current_etl_run, where the old code would have climbed every run.

The API-key guard IS enforcing on the live revision (re-probed 2026-10-01): an unauthenticated business endpoint returns 401 and a non-existent path returns 401 rather than 404, which is only possible when a key is configured (app/api/security.py:35-36 passes through when none is), so FACTORY_API_KEY is provisioned. NOT VERIFIED: the authenticated success path against the live secret, because the probe sent no credential. It is covered in tests/test_api_key_auth.py only. Never write 'the production API is protected'.

NOT verified against the live revision: the BAD/UNKNOWN fail-closed branch was never triggered in the cloud. It is covered at unit and HTTP test level, but no bad data was pushed into a deployed container. REAL_MODEL is also unverified on Azure because no LLM endpoint is reachable from the container, which is why it correctly reports FALLBACK.
No cold-start SLA is claimed: probes timed out at 15s and 60s on scale-from-zero before a 90s-budget warm run succeeded, and the revision template configures no probes.
data/raw/* is gitignored, so the fixture is not in the commit. The 290 figure requires running the generator first. A clean clone cannot reproduce it without that step.
No Airflow or Spark execution was performed. The DAG file and parity tests are covered, but no scheduler or cluster actually ran.

NO BUSINESS CALENDAR. addMinutes (itsm.js:22) is plain wall-clock arithmetic and no business-hours, working-day or holiday helper is exported. A P1 opened Friday 23:00 gets a 15-minute acknowledge target and is breached before anyone is on shift. Every SLA number is 24x7. Recorded as a capability gap rather than a bug, because 24x7 may be the intended policy and the audit cannot tell intent from defect. What it can say is that business-hours SLA support cannot be claimed from here.
No offboarding-workflow test exists, though offboarding appears in 2 other test files.

open_defects.severity: high: false negative in defect inspection

open_defects.defect: Qdrant is required by the primary serving path (build_stack -> QdrantStore, whose constructor hard-probes connectivity and raises), but ACA revision 0000005 provides no QDRANT_URL, so it resolves to localhost:6333. Root cause verified: the ACA deployment is manual and bypasses scripts/deploy.sh, which declares QDRANT_URL REQUIRED. The app starts clean and /health returns 200, so startup success carries no signal about retrieval.
open_defects.fix_direction: Provision a real Qdrant runtime and supply QDRANT_URL through a controlled deployment path FIRST, then make /ready truthful, then negative-test Qdrant loss. Do NOT flip /ready to 503 before Qdrant exists: that yields a permanently unready deployment that still cannot serve retrieval.
open_defects.limitation: Business-path reproduction is NOT_RUN: every retrieval endpoint requires auth and the demo password is in a write-only Azure secret, so the final link is inferred from code rather than observed.

open_defects.defect: JWT_SECRET_KEY is absent on ACA revision 0000005, so the runtime generates an ephemeral random signing key. Tokens and sessions are expected to become invalid after a process restart; with minReplicas=0 every scale-to-zero cycle is a restart.
open_defects.fix_direction: Not to be set by hand. Doing so would add another manually-managed static secret, deepening the problem. Wave 1 must resolve it through identity and a secrets architecture.

open_defects.defect: The deployment contract exists but is not the path actually used. deploy.sh requires QDRANT_URL; .env.example omits it; the build evidence labels the image 'self-contained (no Qdrant)'; ACA runtime has no QDRANT_URL; and there is no ACA deployment automation in the repo.
open_defects.fix_direction: A process defect, not a single missing variable. Fixing QDRANT_URL alone closes this incident while leaving the next required variable free to fail identically. Wave 1 must make the deployment path enforce the contract; Wave 6 must reproduce the environment from code.

resolved_defects.defect: clean_dataframe produced NaN that made the contract validator raise, and the gate failed open, so malformed rows could reach KPI math as a missing quantity
resolved_defects.fix: contract gate made fail-closed: a validator exception is now a DATA_ACCEPTANCE violation, not infrastructure noise. 19 regression tests, one of which is a negative control proving a single bad row still quarantines rather than aborting the file
resolved_defects.was_severity: high: a silent numeric gap in a production ledger

honest_limits: enterprise_score is null for every project. A single score across a vision system, an ETL pipeline and an ERP would hide exactly the differences that matter, and no rubric was agreed before the data was collected.

Three of seven projects have no Azure deployment. The Azure column is NOT_RUN for them rather than assumed. A fourth (Helpdesk) was added as live on 2026-10-01 on the strength of a committed read-only probe, but its boundary is narrow: authMode "lab", mock webhook, no credential in the probe.
No project in this matrix is claimed to be production-ready. Each row's limitations are the operative statement about that project.
